judgments.reasoning_cat2: It displaces the original 4.3's calendar-day count, and the commencement date it runs from is qualified by Addendum 4.1's 'pending approval of permits'.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A bonus of 'a sum to be determined' to be 'divided between the key management staff, as determined by the Owner' fixes neither amount nor method, and is close to an unenforceable agreement to agree.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits against Supplementary Condition 7.1.3.1 (changes in the Contract Sum only by Change Order), 8.1.1 (no compensation for off-site personnel) and Addendum 8.1.8 (management costs covered by the Fee).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Current best estimate', 'industry-standard figures', 'as agreed with Owner' and an Owner termination right 'in Owner's sole and absolute discretion' if the Preliminary Budget is not acceptable are all open-ended, and the clause never says what happens if bids exceed the estimate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The discretionary termination right stands beside Article 13 and A201 Article 14's enumerated termination grounds, and the fast-track Change Order pricing scheme competes with 5.2.6, 6.1 and 12.1.5's Guaranteed Maximum Price machinery.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Capable of being prevented through timely notice of an unsafe condition' is a counterfactual test that will be argued about after any emergency.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It carries the same number as the Agreement's 7.7.2, which it narrows, and A201 10.6 permits emergency action at the Contractor's discretion with compensation under Article 7.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Adds a proviso about the absence of collectible insurance being due to the Contractor's failure to maintain insurance; wordy but reasonably definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It duplicates and modifies the Agreement's 7.7.3 and interacts with 8.1.6, Article 16's blank insurance limits and A201 11.1.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A long enumerated list of items the Fee 'shall cover' ending with the sweeping statement that 'none of these items shall be subject to direct reimbursement under Article 7' — the reach of the list against Article 7's specifics is exactly a general-versus-specific problem.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Article 7 expressly reimburses several of the same categories (7.5.4 telephone, postage, facsimiles; 7.6.6 data processing; 7.2.2-7.2.3 administrative personnel), and it also reuses the number of the original 8.1.8 on the Guaranteed Maximum Price.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A clear notice-and-opportunity condition before the Contractor may take discounts for itself.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Builds on Paragraph 9.1's allocation rule, which it expressly references; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'All in form and substance satisfactory to Owner and Architect' makes payment documentation subject to an unmeasured satisfaction standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It reuses the number 12.1.4 already occupied by the Agreement's substantiation provision, so both must be read together.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A detailed but definite list of what the subcontractor statement must show.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Article 11 accounting records and A201 9.3.1; no conflict located.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It requires executed lien waivers 'establishing payment or satisfaction' of amounts included in the very application for which payment has not yet been made — a timing paradox on the face of the clause.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: A201 9.3.3 and 9.10.2 set out the ordinary sequence of title warranty and final releases, and Addendum 12.2.2 keys final payment to a lien-free title endorsement.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Such other information, documentation, and material as Owner or the Architect reasonably may require' is a catch-all appended to two enumerated specifics, with only 'reasonably' to bound it.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It duplicates the Agreement 12.1.4's 'any other evidence required by the Owner or Architect' and A201 9.3.1's 'such data substantiating the Contractor's right to payment'.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Fixes retainage at five percent and repeats the alternative fee computations without saying which applies to a lump-sum fee.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It replaces the 'N/A' retainage in the Agreement's 12.1.7.3 and sits beside 12.1.8's not-less-than-ten-percent subcontractor retainage.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single added condition to final payment, clearly stated.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It adds a third condition to 12.2.1 and drives the fifty-day clock in Addendum 12.2.2, but nothing in the Agreement obliges anyone to record the Notice.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Two alternative triggers joined by 'whichever is earlier', one of which (a lien-free title endorsement) depends on third-party action.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It displaces the Agreement's 12.2.2 thirty-day rule and must be reconciled with 12.2.3's seven-day final certificate timetable and A201 9.10.1.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Mr. or Mrs. Paul Stephens or Mary Williamson' leaves it open whether any one of them may bind the Owner alone.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Supplementary Condition 2.1.1.1 names Mary Williamson as the authorized representative but allows action by Paul H. Stephens, Elle M. Stephens or Mary Williamson, a third formulation of the same office.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A survival and materiality lead-in to the warranties; conventional.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with A201 1.5.2, 3.2.1 and 13.4.1 on cumulative remedies.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A solvency warranty covering both the Contractor and unnamed Subcontractors, which the Contractor cannot fully know; the subparagraph is also mislabelled '(3)' for '(a)'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: A201 2.2.1 imposes the mirror-image financial-evidence duty on the Owner; the two are complementary rather than conflicting.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Sufficient experience and competence' is a soft warranty standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its promise to furnish tools and equipment sits awkwardly with Article 7 and Exhibits A and C, which let the Contractor charge for the same tools and equipment.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A licensing warranty in definite terms.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with A201 3.7.1-3.7.2 compliance duties; no internal conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A site-visit and familiarity representation in standard form.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It duplicates A201 1.5.2 and 3.2.1 and must be read with A201 4.3.4's relief for concealed or unknown conditions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Identifies the Agreement as modified by the First Addendum; plain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Coherent with the Addendum's incorporation recital; no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Identifies the 1997 A201 as modified by the Supplementary Conditions; plain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It contradicts the Agreement's 15.1.2, which calls the General Conditions 'the 1991 edition', so the two enumerations disagree.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A straightforward incorporation of A201 Articles 1 through 14.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Article 1 of the Agreement gives the Agreement precedence over inconsistent documents, so the incorporation is not unqualified.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The sentence says that when a paragraph 'is modified or deleted by these Supplementary Conditions, the unaltered provision of the General Conditions shall remain in effect' — as written it preserves the very provision it says is deleted, a mechanical defect that inverts the intended meaning.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It governs every clash between the Supplementary Conditions and A201 (for example the two versions of 2.4.1 at c131 and c168), so the error propagates through the instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It converts every Architect approval into an Owner approval while denying the Owner any responsibility 'notwithstanding any of the rights and authority granted the Owner', a broad disclaimer against an equally broad grant.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: A201 4.2.1-4.2.13 vest interpretive and certifying authority in the Architect and A201 4.2.2/4.2.3 disclaim Owner control, so the reallocation of consent rights has to be harmonised across Article 4.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Better quality or greater quantity' and 'more stringent requirement', resolved 'in accordance with the Architect's interpretation as approved by the Owner', is a one-sided conflict rule whose application is contestable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Agreement Article 1 says that where the other Contract Documents are inconsistent with the Agreement, the Agreement governs — a different and potentially opposite resolution rule.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A conventional precedence rule for dimensions and drawing scales.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with A201 1.2.1; no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'No extra charge or compensation will be allowed on account of differences between actual dimensions and the dimensions indicated on the Drawings' is absolute, yet the same paragraph tells the Contractor to submit differences for resolution before proceeding.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: A201 3.2.1-3.2.3 say the Contractor's review is not for the purpose of discovering errors and that it is not liable for Document errors it did not recognise, and A201 4.3.4 allows equitable adjustment for differing conditions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Sufficiently detailed drawings' and 'minor change ... due to actual field conditions' are undefined thresholds.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: A201 7.4.1 gives the Architect authority to order minor changes by written order, a different route for the same subject.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The clause names one authorized representative (Mary Williamson) and then permits binding action by three different people, an internal inconsistency in two consecutive sentences.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Agreement 14.3 and Addendum 14.3 [Revised] give still different lists, and 14.5 requires ten days' notice to change a representative.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single seven-day cure period followed by Owner self-help, clearly expressed.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: A201 2.4.1 (reproduced at c168) requires a second seven-day notice before the Owner may act; the two versions of the same numbered paragraph flatly differ, and Supplementary Condition c124's savings sentence muddies which survives.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A 'detailed timetable of all activities and events' that is 'deemed attached to Document A111 as a part of the Contract Documents' as it is developed — a document that becomes binding without execution.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Phase-based revisions with cost estimates that 'shall become part of the Contract Documents'; the effect of an estimate becoming a Contract Document is unstated.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Supplementary Condition 7.1.3.1 says the Contract Sum may change only by Change Order, and Addendum 6.5 has its own Preliminary Budget procedure, so three provisions govern the same pricing evolution.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A shop-drawing approval and competence warranty; 'if required by the Architect or the Owner or applicable law' is a clear trigger.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: A201 3.12.10 says the Contractor is not required to provide professional design services unless specified, which this clause partly cuts across.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Detailed pleading requirements for time claims; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Supplements A201 4.3.7.1-4.3.7.2 consistently.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The sentence is garbled ('for each aie of the number of causes of delay') and the concurrent-delay rule it states cannot be read with confidence.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: A201 8.3.1 grants extensions for delays beyond the Contractor's control without a concurrency rule, so the two must be reconciled.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It bars claims based on course of conduct, implied acceptance and unjust enrichment 'whether or not there is, in fact, any unjust enrichment', a sweeping one-sided bar whose reach over extra work performed at the Owner's direction is contestable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: A201 7.3 (Construction Change Directives), 7.4 (minor changes by written order), 4.3.4 (concealed conditions) and Addendum 6.5's evolving pricing all allow adjustments without a signed Change Order.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Final settlement of all matters relating to the change ... including all direct and indirect costs' is a broad accord whose reach over later impact and delay claims is a familiar battleground.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: A201 4.3.7 and 7.3.8-7.3.9 contemplate later adjustments and interim determinations, which this finality rule curtails.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'In their sole discretion' joint-check right with express disclaimers of privity; clearly drafted.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: A201 9.6.2 requires the Contractor to pay Subcontractors out of amounts received, and 9.6.4 disclaims any Owner obligation to Subcontractors, which this dovetails with.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Conditions the final Certificate on all warranties being 'received and accepted by the Owner', with acceptance unqualified by any reasonableness standard.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A clear exclusion of tools and construction equipment from the Owner's property insurance, with a waiver-of-subrogation requirement.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: A201 11.4.1 requires all-risk insurance on the Work including materials, and 11.4.7's waiver of subrogation extends to property insurance 'applicable to the Work', so the boundary of covered property matters.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'All reasonable costs (including attorneys' fees and court and settlement expenses) properly attributable thereto' is a fee-shifting formula with an elastic attribution test.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It duplicates A201 11.4.1.2's remedy for the Owner's failure to insure and interacts with A201 4.3.10's waiver of consequential damages and Article 16's blank insurance limits.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The exhibit says hand-tool cost 'shall be borne by the Contractor' and in the very next sentence adds a flat 5% of payroll to cover those same tools; the illustrative list ('include, but are not limited to ... air compressors ... beam saws ... etc.') also stretches 'hand tools' well beyond its ordinary sense.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Agreement 7.5.1 reimburses only tools 'fully consumed' with salvage credits, 8.1.5 excludes rental costs of machinery except under 7.5.2, and 8.1.7 excludes any cost not expressly described in Article 7 — none of which authorises a percentage markup.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It fixes the general liability premium 'at the rate of 1% of the total labor and subcontractors' costs' — a formula that bears no necessary relation to premium actually paid, and 'labor and subcontractors' costs' is undefined.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Agreement 7.6.1 reimburses only 'that portion of insurance and bond premiums that can be directly attributed to this Contract', and 8.1.7 bars costs not expressly described in Article 7.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It defines 'Subcontract' costs, then extends the definition to unnamed 'certain vendors' costs ... including; rubbish hauling and tipping fees, engineering and consulting fees, temporary facilities fees, freight charges, etc.' — an enumerated list closed with 'etc.' whose reach cannot be fixed.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Agreement 7.6.2 reimburses taxes 'imposed by a governmental authority that are related to the Work' without this exclusion scheme, and 8.1.7 limits costs to Article 7 items.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A definitional list of Contract Documents and Modifications; conventional and closed-ended.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Entire-agreement and no-privity provisions in standard form; 'may be amended or modified only by Modification' is definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Supplementary Condition 7.1.3.1 reinforces it, but Supplementary Conditions 3.10.4 and 3.10.5 let schedules and cost estimates become Contract Documents without a Modification.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'The Work' is defined broadly to include 'all other labor, materials, equipment and services provided or to be provided by the Contractor to fulfill the Contractor's obligations'.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short definition of the Project; standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with A201 6.1 on separate contracts.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A definition of the Drawings; plain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 15.1.5 of the Agreement lists no Drawings, so what qualifies is left to extrinsic proof.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A conventional definition of the Specifications; nothing elastic.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Agreement 15.1.4 identifies the Specifications only by reference to an undated Project Manual, so the definition has no fixed referent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'A volume assembled for the Work which may include' bidding requirements and Conditions is permissive but harmless.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Agreement 15.1.3 leaves the Project Manual date as 'TBD' while 15.1.4 defines the Specifications by it, so the definition points to an unidentified volume.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Complementary, and what is required by one shall be as binding as if required by all' combined with performance 'reasonably inferable' from the Documents is a classic scope-of-work standard that parties read differently.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Agreement Article 1 gives the Agreement precedence over inconsistent documents and Supplementary Condition 1.2.1.1 imposes the more stringent requirement, so three different reconciliation rules coexist.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short rule that specification organisation does not control trade division; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 5.2.1 and Agreement 10.1 on subcontracting.

judgments.reasoning_cat2: It bears on contested trade terms elsewhere, notably 'hand tools' in 7.5.1 and Exhibit C, but is not itself inconsistent with any provision.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A capitalisation convention; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent throughout; no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An interpretive rule about omitted modifiers and articles that itself tells courts to disregard textual differences — unusual, but clear in purpose.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It supports harmonising the varied wording across the Agreement, Addendum and Supplementary Conditions; no conflict located.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Requires the parties to sign the Contract Documents and provides for identification of unsigned ones; definite.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A standard site-visit representation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It duplicates Addendum 14.6(d) and must be read with A201 4.3.4's relief for unknown conditions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A long but carefully drafted copyright and instruments-of-service provision.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Concerns the Architect's rights and does not interact with the payment or scope provisions; no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The scanned text is fragmentary and the obligation (record legal title information within fifteen days of written request) can only be partly reconstructed from it.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Relates to Agreement 4.1's provision for the Owner's time to file mortgages and mechanic's liens; consistent in substance.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Reasonable evidence that financial arrangements have been made' as a 'condition precedent to commencement or continuation of the Work' is an undefined sufficiency standard with drastic consequences.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: A201 14.1.1.4 lets the Contractor terminate for failure to furnish this evidence, and Addendum 6.5 gives the Owner a discretionary termination right, so the entry and exit conditions interact.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Allocates easements, assessments and charges to the Owner except permits and fees under 3.7.1; clear division.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Owner furnishes surveys and legal description; Contractor may rely but must exercise care.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 3.2.1 and 4.3.4; no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Such copies ... as are reasonably necessary' is a modest standard in a minor provision.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Agreement 7.5.4 makes document reproduction a reimbursable cost, which overlaps the free-of-charge promise.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Persistently fails' is a soft trigger, but the remedy and its limits are clearly stated.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Read with 2.4.1 (in both its A201 and Supplementary Conditions forms) and 12.2; the stop-work right is separate and consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A two-stage seven-day notice procedure, spelled out in detail.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A definition of the Contractor; nothing to construe.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single-sentence performance obligation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Mirrors Agreement Article 2 and its Addendum revision; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short non-relief provision; definite.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It requires careful study and comparison yet says the obligations 'are not for the purpose of discovering errors, omissions, or inconsistencies' — a much-argued pair of sentences about how far a contractor must look.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short compliance obligation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 3.7.3-3.7.4 and 10.2.2.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Knowing it to be contrary to laws' and 'appropriate responsibility' are judgment-laden but standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Complements 3.7.3 and 8.1.6's exclusion of costs due to the Contractor's failures.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'A competent superintendent and necessary assistants' with communications to him binding the Contractor; conventional.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Review-and-submit duties with 'reasonable promptness'; standard.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A narrow procedural rule about resubmittals.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A waiver of the Owner's Claims subject to three enumerated exceptions — the scope of a waiver defined by exceptions is a standing source of dispute.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Addendum 14.6 says the Contractor's warranties survive final completion and Agreement 12.2.5 contemplates post-final-payment correction work, so the waiver's reach is qualified elsewhere.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Acceptance of final payment waives all Claims 'except those previously made in writing and identified by that payee as unsettled at the time of final Application for Payment' — a forfeiture turning on the form and timing of earlier writings.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Agreement 12.2.4 gives the Contractor a separate 30-day arbitration right after the final Certificate while requiring the Owner to pay the certified amount, so acceptance of that payment and preservation of the dispute sit awkwardly together.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line allocation of safety responsibility.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Reinforced by Supplementary Condition 1.1.2.1's Owner disclaimer; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Reasonable precautions' and 'reasonable protection' introduce an enumerated list of protected interests; standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 10.2.2-10.2.3 and 3.18 indemnity.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A notice and compliance obligation in definite terms.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 3.7.2; no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Reasonable safeguards ... as required by existing conditions and performance of the Contract' with an illustrative list; conventional.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 10.1.1 and 10.2.1.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The sentence is truncated in this copy, and 'utmost care' for explosives and 'unusual methods' are undefined standards.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Relates to 10.3 hazardous materials and 3.18 indemnity; no conflict located.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Designation of a responsible safety member, presumed to be the superintendent; clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 3.9.1 and Addendum Article 2 [Revised] each require designated personnel, so three provisions govern who is in charge on site.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short prohibition on overloading.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 10.2.1; no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'If reasonable precautions will be inadequate to prevent foreseeable bodily injury or death' from 'a material or substance, including but not limited to asbestos or polychlorinated biphenyl' is a predictive standard attached to an open-ended list.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 10.4 excepts materials brought to the site by the Contractor, and Addendum 7.7.2 [Revision] narrows emergency cost recovery, so the allocation of hazard risk is spread across provisions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A detailed procedure ending in an extension of Contract Time and increase in the Contract Sum for 'reasonable additional costs of shut-down, delay and start-up'; the cost categories are the loose part.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 4.3.10's waiver of consequential damages and Supplementary Condition 7.1.3.1's Change-Order-only rule constrain this remedy.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An Owner indemnity qualified by 'to the fullest extent permitted by law' and defeated only by 'the sole negligence of a party seeking indemnity' — familiar but contested wording.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is the mirror of 3.18.1's Contractor indemnity and must be read with 11.4.7's waiver of subrogation and the blank Article 16 insurance terms.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Unless such materials or substances were required by the Contract Documents' is a clean exception.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Qualifies 10.3.1-10.3.3; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Emergency action 'at the Contractor's discretion' with compensation determined under 4.3 and Article 7; clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Addendum 7.7.2 [Revision] denies reimbursement for emergencies caused by the Contractor or preventable by timely notice, which qualifies the compensation this clause promises.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An eight-item enumerated schedule of claims to be insured; detailed and closed.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Article 16 of the Agreement, which is supposed to state required limits, is blank, and Exhibits D and E supply only a premium rate and a certificate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Not less than limits of liability specified in the Contract Documents or required by law, whichever coverage is greater' presupposes specified limits, and the comparison itself is awkward.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Article 16 states no limits at all, so the benchmark this clause depends on is missing from the instrument and only Exhibit E's certificate supplies figures.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Certificates 'acceptable to the Owner' plus a 30-day cancellation notice requirement; standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Exhibit E is a certificate of liability insurance which by its own terms confers no rights and does not amend the policies, and Article 16 states no requirements to measure it against.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'The Owner's usual liability insurance' is undefined as to type, scope and limits — a term whose content cannot be fixed from the contract.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Article 16 is blank and 11.4 assigns property insurance to the Owner, so what the Owner must carry is left almost entirely open.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Optionally, the Owner may require' insurance that then triggers a Contract Sum increase; whether the option was exercised is a pure fact question the clause does not answer.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 3.18.1's indemnity is expressly limited 'to the extent claims ... are not covered by Project Management Protective Liability insurance purchased by the Contractor', so the indemnity's scope depends on this optional coverage that Article 16 never addresses.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The text is truncated mid-sentence, and it waives 'all rights against each other for damages' to the extent covered by insurance that may never have been purchased.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It interlocks with 3.18.1's indemnity and 11.4.7's subrogation waiver, and Article 16 leaves the optional coverage unaddressed.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A flat prohibition on requiring additional insureds; clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Exhibit E's certificate and Supplementary Condition 11.4.1.1.1's insurance arrangements bear on the same subject, and Article 16 is silent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It requires all-risk cover 'in the amount of the initial Contract Sum plus value of subsequent Contract modifications' and 'without optional deductibles' — an amount that presupposes a fixed initial sum.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: This is a cost-plus contract with an 'N/A' Guaranteed Maximum Price and no stated Contract Sum, and 11.4.1.3 contemplates deductibles this clause says are not to be taken.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An enumerated list of perils 'without limitation', which leaves the outer edge of covered risks open.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Supplementary Condition 11.4.1.1.1 removes tools and construction equipment from the Owner's cover, narrowing this list.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A clear fallback if the Owner does not insure, including a Change Order for the Contractor's substitute cover.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Supplementary Condition 11.6 states an overlapping remedy for either party's failure to insure, including attorneys' fees, so two remedies address the same default.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line deductible allocation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 11.4.1 requires the policy to be written 'without optional deductibles', so the two sentences pull in different directions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short extension of cover to stored and in-transit Work.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Supplementary Condition 11.4.1.1.1 excludes tools and equipment not included in the Work, and Agreement 7.5.6/12.1.7.2 govern off-site storage approvals.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Conditions partial occupancy on insurer consent and forbids unilateral action risking cancellation; clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 9.9 and 11.4.1.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Boiler and machinery insurance 'required in the Contract Documents or by law'; the requirement is conditional on documents elsewhere.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Article 16 states no insurance requirements at all, so the condition may never be satisfied.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The Owner 'waives all rights of action against the Contractor for loss of use of the Owner's property, including consequential losses due to fire or other hazards however caused' — an extremely broad waiver keyed to insurance the Owner 'may' purchase.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It overlaps 4.3.10's mutual consequential-damages waiver and 11.4.7's subrogation waiver while cutting against 3.18.1's indemnity in favour of the Owner.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A conditional waiver tied to separate property policies; detailed and definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Depends on 11.4.7's waiver machinery; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Requires the Owner to file policies with the Contractor before exposure to loss; clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 11.4.1.2 contemplates the Owner not purchasing at all, so this filing duty may be inoperative in the same circumstances.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A sweeping mutual waiver 'to the extent covered by property insurance obtained pursuant to this Paragraph 11.4 or other property insurance applicable to the Work', effective even where a duty of indemnification exists — the interaction of those clauses is heavily argued.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It must be reconciled with 3.18.1's indemnity, 11.4.3's loss-of-use waiver and Supplementary Condition 11.4.1.1.1's carve-out of tools and equipment.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An Owner-as-fiduciary adjustment mechanism, but it cross-refers to 'Subparagraph 11.4.10', which is not among the incorporated provisions here.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Depends on the Owner having purchased 11.4.1 property insurance, which 11.4.1.2 allows it not to do.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The correction obligation and the cost-bearing sentence are badly scrambled in this copy, making the allocation of testing and Architect's-services costs hard to read.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Agreement 7.6.4 excludes laboratory fees for defective Work from reimbursement and 8.1.6 excludes negligence costs, which align with this allocation.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The sentence is incomplete as reproduced ('shall be extended with ... by the period of time'), so the extension rule cannot be applied as written.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It works with 12.2.2.3 and 13.7.1's limitation accrual, both of which depend on the length of the correction period.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: As reproduced it reads 'The one-year period for correction of Work shall not be performed by the Contractor pursuant to this Paragraph 12.2', which is nonsense — words have plainly dropped out and the intended rule (no extension by corrective Work) is not what the text says.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 12.2.2.2 states the opposite extension rule and 13.7.1 keys limitation accrual to these periods, so the defect matters beyond this sentence.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The text is garbled but its point — that the one-year correction period is not a limitation on other obligations or on the time for enforcement — is a much-argued proposition about warranty periods.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 13.7.1 fixes accrual dates for limitation purposes and 3.5's warranty runs separately, so three provisions govern how long liability lasts.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'The law of the place where the Project is located' is definite here (Hawaii).
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 4.5.3's mediation venue and the Project description; no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The text is badly scrambled and the assignment restriction ('neither party ... shall assign the Contract as a whole without written consent of the other') can only be partially reconstructed.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Agreement 13.3 and A201 5.4 require assignments of subcontracts on termination, which this restriction expressly excepts in its intact form.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Only a fragment survives ('rights and remedies ... a limitation of duties, obligations, rights and'), so the cumulative-remedies rule cannot be read from the text.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Cumulative remedies bear on the waivers in 4.3.10, 9.10.4-9.10.5 and 11.4.7, which are stated as exclusive in places.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The provision survives only in fragments, leaving the testing and inspection obligations largely illegible.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Agreement 7.6.4 addresses reimbursement of laboratory fees and 13.5.5-13.5.6 the conduct of tests; the substance is consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Promptly and, where practicable, at the normal place of testing'; a modest standard in a short duty.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 13.5.6 and 4.2.2.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Made promptly to avoid unreasonable delay in the Work' is a familiar standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 13.5.5 and 8.3.1.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A three-part deemed-accrual rule for statutes of limitation, partly corrupted in this copy, whose validity and effect on latent-defect claims are perennially contested.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 12.2.5 says the correction period has no relationship to the time within which obligations may be enforced, and 4.6.3 ties arbitration deadlines to 'the applicable statute of limitations as determined pursuant to Paragraph 13.7'.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Four enumerated grounds for Contractor termination after a 30-day stoppage; the grounds are specific.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Agreement 13.1 caps what the Contractor may recover on such a termination by reference to the 13.2 for-cause formula, a different measure from A201 14.1.3.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The threshold is garbled and internally odd — suspensions aggregating 'more than 100 percent of the total number of days scheduled for completion, or 120 days in any 365-day period, whichever is less' — so the trigger cannot be applied with confidence.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 14.3 permits suspension for convenience 'for such period of time as the Owner may determine', which this is meant to limit.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Persistently failed to fulfill the Owner's obligations ... with respect to matters important to the progress of the Work' is an accumulation of undefined qualifiers.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It overlaps 14.1.1's grounds and 9.7.1's stop-work right, and the recovery it points to (14.1.3) is capped by Agreement 13.1.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Three specific grounds are followed by '.4 otherwise is guilty of substantial breach of a provision of the Contract Documents' — an open catch-all after enumerated specifics, and 'persistently or repeatedly' is itself imprecise.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Agreement 13.2 caps the amount payable on such a termination by reference to a Guaranteed Maximum Price that does not exist, and Addendum 6.5 gives the Owner a separate discretionary termination right.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Requires Architect certification that sufficient cause exists and lists three Owner remedies; 'whatever reasonable method the Owner may deem expedient' is the loose phrase.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Supplementary Condition 1.1.2.1 layers Owner consent onto Architect functions, and Agreement 13.2 limits the resulting payment; 5.4.1's contingent assignment is also triggered here.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The computation turns on 'the unpaid balance of the Contract Sum' compared with the Owner's finishing costs and damages; the arithmetic is clear but the inputs are not.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: There is no fixed Contract Sum or Guaranteed Maximum Price in this cost-plus Agreement, and Agreement 13.2 imposes its own cap on what may be paid to the Contractor.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Suspension 'without cause ... for such period of time as the Owner may determine' is an unbounded discretion.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 14.1.2 limits cumulative suspensions and Agreement 13.4 provides for the resulting Guaranteed Maximum Price and Time increases, a price that does not exist here.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'At any time ... for the Owner's convenience and without cause' is about as definite as a termination right can be.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Agreement 13.1 caps recovery on such a termination well below A201 14.4.3's measure, and Addendum 6.5 adds a further 'sole and absolute discretion' termination right, so the exit rights are stated in three inconsistent ways.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Three enumerated duties on receipt of a convenience-termination notice; clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Works with 5.4.1's contingent assignment and Agreement 13.3's assignment obligation.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Payment for Work executed, and costs incurred by reason of such termination, along with reasonable overhead and profit on the Work not executed' is broad, and 'reasonable overhead and profit' is undefined in a contract that pays a fixed Fee.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Agreement 13.1 expressly caps the amount payable under this subparagraph at what the Contractor could recover under 13.2, and Agreement 6.3 redefines 'profit' as the Contractor's Fee, so this promise and the Agreement's cap conflict.
